We need to find template that when applied to the given molecule reproduces the HWE reaction (phosphonate to alkene). The given molecule appears to be a product of HWE: an alkene attached to a phosphonate? Actually product is an alkene with a phosphonate group? The SMILES: C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO

It has a C=C double bond attached to a carbon bearing OCH2? Actually it's a vinyl ether? The HWE reaction forms an alkene from aldehyde/ketone + phosphonate carbanion, giving alkene and a phosphonate byproduct? Wait typical HWE: Phosphonate + aldehyde -> alkene + phosphate (byproduct). The product is alkene, the phosphonate becomes a phosphate (P=O). In our product, there is a phosphonate group attached to a carboxylic acid? Actually there is O[Si] group etc. Might be a protected phosphonate? The template likely breaks a C-P bond and a C-O bond, forming C=C and carboxylic acid.

We need to retrieve template ID and mapped_rxn. We can search template catalog by criteria: functional_groups_broken maybe "phosphonate"? Not in list. The functional groups list includes "phosphonate"? Not listed. So maybe we need to search by bonds broken/formed. Bonds broken: P-C and C-O (the C-O of the phosphonate? maybe O-P?). Bonds formed: C=C. Also functional groups formed: aliphatic carboxylic acid, C-C double bonds.

But bonds format expects atomic numbers: e.g., "6-6" for C-C, "6-8" for C-O, "6-15" for C-P? Phosphorus atomic number 15. So broken bonds: "6-15" (C-P) and "6-8" (C-O). Formed bond: "6-6" (C=C). Let's try search.
